_readme: Curated index for articles/index.html, lifted out of the hand-maintained page on 2026-08-13. `sections` is the editorial running order of card groups; per article, `label` is the card eyebrow and `summary` is the hand-written card blurb (deliberately NOT the meta description). `showUpdated: true` appends a live "Updated <month year>" derived from the article dateModified -- the date is never stored here, so it cannot go stale. Rendered by scripts/generate_articles_index.js (npm run articles:index) into articles/index.html between the article-cards markers; the surrounding page shell stays hand-maintained. An article with no entry here still appears, under UNSORTED, using its own title/description.

what-is-legislationpatch.html.label: About LegislationPatch
what-is-legislationpatch.html.summary: LegislationPatch tracks U.S. federal legislation and translates bill text into plain English — bill text and status from the Congress.gov API, floor statements from the Congressional Record on GovInfo, roll calls from the House Clerk and the Senate.

methodology.html.label: Methodology
methodology.html.summary: Where our data comes from, how we read a bill, the patch notes format, what we deliberately don't do, and the limits of our analysis.

plain-english-government.html.label: About LegislationPatch
plain-english-government.html.summary: Federal legislation is publicly available — but functionally inaccessible. The gap between availability and accessibility has real political consequences.

how-to-read-a-bill.html.label: Guide
how-to-read-a-bill.html.summary: Federal bills follow a predictable structure. This guide explains each part — the enacting clause, section numbering, amendment language, and how to find what actually changed.

how-a-bill-becomes-law.html.label: Explainer
how-a-bill-becomes-law.html.summary: Every step from the hopper to the presidential pen, checked against the rules that define it — including the two routes to the House floor that need no rule from the Rules Committee, and what budget reconciliation actually limits.

what-is-a-committee.html.label: Explainer
what-is-a-committee.html.summary: Most bills introduced in Congress never get a hearing, a vote, or any action. They die in committee. Here's how the committee system works and why it holds that much power.

what-is-congressional-record.html.label: Explainer
what-is-congressional-record.html.summary: The official record of House and Senate proceedings, published since 1873. What its four sections contain, what “revise and extend” actually permits, how much weight courts give a floor statement, and what our own quote stores do and do not record.

legislative-stages.html.label: Explainer
legislative-stages.html.summary: A bill's stage says which steps it has completed, not how likely it is to finish. What each stage is under the House rules, the enrollment statutes and Article I — and what the stage and likelihood on a LegislationPatch bill card do and do not mean.

save-america-act.html.label: Bill Tracker
save-america-act.html.summary: H.R. 7296 would require documentary proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote in federal elections. Still in committee as of August 2026, but its text has been attached to two other bills; distinct from the SAVE Act, H.R. 22.

kids-online-safety-act.html.label: Bill Tracker
kids-online-safety-act.html.summary: S. 1748 would impose a duty of care on online platforms used by minors. The Senate Commerce Committee ordered it reported with a substitute that has not been published; a predecessor package passed the Senate 91-3 in July 2024.

ndaa-fy2027.html.label: Bill Tracker
ndaa-fy2027.html.summary: H.R. 8800, the FY2027 defense authorization bill, passed the House 216-212 on July 22, 2026, after a second rule cleared the way for it 214-211.

ndaa-fy2026.html.label: Bill Tracker
ndaa-fy2026.html.summary: S. 2296, the FY2026 defense authorization bill, passed the Senate 77-20 on October 9, 2025 and was held at the desk in the House. It never became law: the FY2026 NDAA was enacted through a different vehicle, S. 1071, as Public Law 119-60.

safe-drugs-act.html.label: Bill Tracker
safe-drugs-act.html.summary: H.R. 6509 would tighten federal oversight of drug compounding and set new limits on compounded copies of commercially available drugs. Still in committee as of August 2026, but the related Senate bill is on the Senate calendar.

fisa-surveillance-tracker.html.label: Bill Tracker
fisa-surveillance-tracker.html.summary: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lapsed on June 12, 2026 — its first lapse since 2008. Complete tracker of every 2026 extension — bill text, votes, and how the authority ultimately lapsed.

holocaust-art-recovery.html.label: Bill Analysis · Pub. L. 119-82
holocaust-art-recovery.html.summary: S. 1884, signed April 13, 2026, permanently removed the procedural defenses U.S. courts had used to dismiss Holocaust art restitution claims without reaching the merits.

appropriations-act-2026.html.label: Bill Analysis · FY2026
appropriations-act-2026.html.summary: H.R. 7148 became Public Law 119-75 on February 3, 2026, carrying five of the twelve annual appropriations acts for fiscal year 2026 — days after a lapse in appropriations its own text records.

small-business-innovation-act.html.label: Bill Analysis · Pub. L. 119-83
small-business-innovation-act.html.summary: S. 3971, signed April 13, 2026, extended SBIR and STTR grant programs through FY2031 and added mandatory screening against eight federal watchlists for foreign adversary ties.

blm-land-withdrawal.html.label: Bill Analysis · CRA Disapproval
blm-land-withdrawal.html.summary: H.J.Res. 140, signed April 27, 2026, cancelled the BLM's 20-year mining ban on 225,504 acres of Minnesota National Forest bordering the Boundary Waters.

e15-ethanol-waiver.html.label: Bill Analysis · In Progress
e15-ethanol-waiver.html.summary: H.R. 1346 would allow year-round E15 sales by extending the E10 Reid Vapor Pressure waiver to E15, removing the current summer ozone-season prohibition.

women-lung-cancer-act.html.label: Bill Analysis · In Progress
women-lung-cancer-act.html.summary: H.R. 2319 would direct HHS to conduct an interagency review of lung cancer research gaps for women and underserved populations and report findings to Congress.

fire-act-wildfire.html.label: Bill Analysis · In Progress
fire-act-wildfire.html.summary: H.R. 6387 would require EPA to revise its exceptional events regulations within 18 months and extend them to prescribed burns and similar State approved wildfire mitigation. Sponsors say it shields communities from air-quality penalties they attribute to wildfire smoke; opponents say it would weaken the NAAQS program.

119th-congress-tracker.html.label: Tracker
119th-congress-tracker.html.summary: The complete roster of 119th Congress bills in our database on one page — every signed law, chamber passage, and failed vote, plus the funding and FISA deadlines to watch.

fisa-history.html.label: History
fisa-history.html.summary: Section 702 has been reauthorized or extended six times since 2008. Complete history — every major action, what changed, and what the pattern reveals about the politics of surveillance reauthorization.

what-is-cbo.html.label: Explainer
what-is-cbo.html.summary: The Congressional Budget Act tells the CBO exactly what a cost estimate must contain, over what horizon, and against what baseline. What the statute requires, and what CBO does and does not price.

senate-filibuster.html.label: Explainer
senate-filibuster.html.summary: A filibuster is any tactic that keeps a Senate measure from coming to a vote. Cloture under Rule XXII is the only rule that can end debate, and it carries three different thresholds.

government-shutdown.html.label: Explainer
government-shutdown.html.summary: A government shutdown follows a funding gap. What the Antideficiency Act requires, which functions are excepted rather than essential, who decides what stops, and how long the gaps have actually lasted.

budget-reconciliation.html.label: Explainer
budget-reconciliation.html.summary: Reconciliation limits Senate debate time, so cloture is never needed to reach a final vote. How the directives work, what the Byrd rule bars, and which laws lost their short titles to it.

house-rules-committee.html.label: Explainer
house-rules-committee.html.summary: The House Rules Committee controls which bills reach the floor, how long debate lasts, and what amendments are allowed. Its majority is appointed by the Speaker.

presidential-veto.html.label: Explainer
presidential-veto.html.summary: The President can reject legislation by returning it with objections. Congress can override with a two-thirds majority — a threshold that's rarely achieved.

continuing-resolution.html.label: Explainer
continuing-resolution.html.summary: A continuing resolution temporarily funds the government when regular appropriations haven't passed. Here's how CRs work and why they've become the default mode of federal budgeting.

appropriations-process.html.label: Explainer
appropriations-process.html.summary: Twelve annual appropriations bills fund the operations of most federal agencies, one per Appropriations subcommittee. All twelve have been enacted before the fiscal year started four times since FY1977, most recently for FY1997.

cloture-60-vote.html.label: Explainer
cloture-60-vote.html.summary: Cloture is the only Senate rule that can end debate without rejecting the matter being debated. Rule XXII sets three thresholds, not one, and a post-cloture time cap that can only be increased.

congressional-oversight.html.label: Explainer
congressional-oversight.html.summary: Congressional oversight is Congress's power to investigate, subpoena, and review executive branch conduct. Here's what tools Congress has and what its limits are.

signing-statements.html.label: Explainer
signing-statements.html.summary: Signing statements explain how the President will interpret a new law and sometimes signal which provisions won't be enforced. Here's their legal status and history.

unanimous-consent.html.label: Explainer
unanimous-consent.html.summary: Party leaders and other senators propound unanimous consent requests every day the Senate is in session. A simple request and a negotiated agreement are two different things, and one objection defeats either.

pocket-veto.html.label: Explainer
pocket-veto.html.summary: A pocket veto occurs when the President takes no action on a bill and Congress adjourns before the 10-day period expires. It is not subject to the override process — and which adjournments produce one is still disputed.

joint-resolution.html.label: Explainer
joint-resolution.html.summary: Not everything Congress passes is a bill. Joint resolutions, concurrent resolutions, and simple resolutions each carry different legal weight and serve different purposes.

bill-numbering.html.label: Explainer
bill-numbering.html.summary: Every measure Congress numbers carries a prefix that signals its type and whether it can become law. A legend for all eight measure types and how the numbers get assigned.

voice-vote-vs-roll-call.html.label: Explainer
voice-vote-vs-roll-call.html.summary: A voice vote, a division vote and unanimous consent all leave no record of who voted. What each method is, the House thresholds for a recorded vote — 44 on the floor, 25 in the Committee of the Whole — and what "agreed to by voice vote" means for the public record.

congressional-review-act.html.label: Explainer
congressional-review-act.html.summary: The Congressional Review Act lets Congress overturn a federal agency rule through a joint resolution of disapproval, using an expedited Senate procedure that cannot be filibustered.

discharge-petition.html.label: Explainer
discharge-petition.html.summary: A discharge petition lets 218 House members force a bill out of committee and onto the floor over the objection of leadership. How the threshold works and how often it succeeds.

impoundment-rescission.html.label: Explainer
impoundment-rescission.html.summary: The Impoundment Control Act sets the rules for when the executive can withhold appropriated funds — rescissions, deferrals, the 45-day clock, the GAO's role, and the disputed pocket rescission.

suspension-of-the-rules.html.label: Explainer
suspension-of-the-rules.html.summary: Suspension of the rules lets the House pass a bill with 40 minutes of debate, no amendments, and a two-thirds vote of the Members voting. What House Rule XV says, which days it is allowed, and what changed in the 119th Congress.

omnibus-vs-minibus.html.label: Explainer
omnibus-vs-minibus.html.summary: An omnibus carries several of the twelve annual appropriations bills in one measure, a minibus carries only some of them, and a continuing resolution carries none. What the terms mean, how the divisions work, and which bills in our database are which.

how-we-source-quotes.html.label: About LegislationPatch
how-we-source-quotes.html.summary: Every member quote is verbatim from the Congressional Record on GovInfo, or it is discarded. Here is the extraction process, the speaker-matching rules, and what provenance each of our two quote stores actually keeps.

how-we-track-voting.html.label: About LegislationPatch
how-we-track-voting.html.summary: Vote data comes directly from the House Clerk and Senate official records, matched to members by bioguide ID in the House and by surname and state in the Senate, with crossover detection on close-margin votes.

legislationpatch-and-ai.html.label: About LegislationPatch
legislationpatch-and-ai.html.summary: How the site is structured so any claim on it can be traced back to its source — verbatim floor quotes, schema.org markup on every article and bill page, and the bill version an analysis was actually written against.

no-editorial-spin.html.label: About LegislationPatch
no-editorial-spin.html.summary: No editorial spin is easy to say and harder to execute. Here's what it means in practice — what we describe, what we don't, and where the line sits between neutral description and political framing.
